cards.title: Sonos Port: native playback fails with ERROR_PLAYBACK_NO_CONTENT, AirPlay volume snaps back
cards.area: server / providers/sonos player.py _on_playback_error, streams controller (port 8097); airplay/player.py volume (with #6664)
cards.summary: 2.10.7 HA add-on, Sonos Port 'Office' (line-out Variable). Native playback fails at once ('Speaker Office could not play None and reported ERROR_PLAYBACK_NO_CONTENT'), with MP3 and radio, Flow mode on and off, publish IP auto or the HA LAN IP. On AirPlay it plays, but volume changes from MA or the Sonos app snap back after a few seconds until MA clears the AirPlay output. Same error as the bot-closed support#5721.
cards.checked: Opus subagent, 2.10.7 = dev on these paths. 'None' is the speaker's own trackName/itemId in the playbackError event (player.py:1028-1034 on 2.10.7), so it failed before resolving any item; no httpStatus, so most likely no HTTP answer from MA. Flow on (play_stream_url) and off (play_cloud_queue) both need the Port to fetch http://<publish_ip>:8097; Sonos app, AirPlay and the browser don't, so likely a reachability problem (VLAN/firewall/port 8097), about 65%. Volume: Port on Variable has VOLUME_SET, so __control_for_output returns NATIVE and owns_volume is False (same as #6664); the Sonos provider doesn't push volume back. MA-side snap-back candidates: AirPlay DACP device-volume > update_volume_from_device > _adopt_device_volume writes VOLUME= back without an owns_volume check (airplay/provider.py:1111-1135, airplay/player.py:828-839, 1031-1044), or _enforce_volume_limits if a min/max volume is set (players/controller.py:2150). 10-22 log (last 1000 lines, to 12:35:01): stream server 192.168.1.134:8097, Port at 192.168.3.10 (other VLAN; reporter: 'gave full access', no min/max volume). SONOS + AirPlay Verbose from 12:31; native at 12:33:40, playbackError ERROR_PLAYBACK_NO_CONTENT at 12:33:50 (serviceId -1), with no 'Cloud Queue request' (provider.py:273, VERBOSE) and no 'Start Queue Flow stream' in between: no queue or flow request reached MA. Streams wasn't Verbose. No volume changes in the captured lines. 10-22 11:51 UTC: reporter: opening http://192.168.1.134:8097 from the Port's VLAN 'will give a timeout'. So the inter-VLAN firewall blocks 192.168.3.x -> 192.168.1.134:8097. 10-28: 'pause, wait ~20 s, then volume works from MA'. No 20 s window in MA (only the 2 s echo window, constants.py:348, player.py:834-843). Likely the paused AirPlay session ending, after which the active output protocol clears (players/controller.py:3140-3143) and native Sonos volume sticks. Snap-back while playing: device-side revert during AirPlay (as salanki saw on #5018) or MA writing DACP reports back via _adopt_device_volume -> volume_set (player.py:845-856, 1048-1061, 681-692) without the owns_volume check the session-start push has (stream.py:387). Needs AirPlay + Sonos Verbose to tell.
cards.plan: If MA-side: record the DACP level without writing it back when the AirPlay leg doesn't own the volume (unit-testable). If device-side: route volume over the AirPlay leg while AirPlay is the active output on Sonos.

cards.area: server / providers/heos player.py, player_queues/queue_loader.py, Spotify Soloist single stream slot
cards.summary: 2.10.7 HA add-on, HEOS native to a Denon AVR-X1700H, Spotify (Soloist), flow mode. A manual skip or picking a queue item often leaves the receiver silent while MA's position keeps moving for 12-14 s, then it stops; Play resumes from the advanced position. cards.checked: Opus subagent, diagnostics only (no debug log). HEOS 'Playback error. Unsupported format.' 6x in pairs, plus 'Spotify has reached its limit of 1 concurrent source streams after waiting 15 seconds' (21:56, 22:15) and 'Spotify is already streaming somewhere else' (22:01, another client on the account took over during tests). The 12-14 s drift is the HEOS start window (5 s, heos/constants.py:36) plus the 10 s stop grace (:38, player.py:520-535), not a separate bug. A skip already hands the slot over (queue_loader.py:376-378, 1233-1256). #6873 doesn't apply, HEOS forces flow mode (player.py:65). Different trigger and error than #6831 (MP3 fails too), though #6831's fix may help the first-bytes delay. 10-23 02:37 UTC panda-star357 (not the reporter): similar on 2.10.7 Docker, single Denon Home 250 fw 3.139.170, native HEOS + QQ Music: after Next the speaker stops ~15 s later; AirPlay to a Samsung Q800B on the same server is fine. His AI-assisted read: an old HEOS queue-cleanup task overlaps a newer play request; his local guard fixed skips but a later 'Unsupported format' still happened. cards.area: server / controllers/streams/controller.py flow route chunk_size, helpers/ffmpeg.py, helpers/process.py
cards.summary: Docker 2.11.0.dev2026100703, native HEOS group of two Denon Home 200s, Tidal, FLAC 44.1/24 output, ICY off, crossfade off. Playback stopped near 434 s of a 466 s track and every Play retried that position and failed with HEOS 'Unable to play media'. An MA restart didn't help, skipping to the next track did. Incident log, diagnostics and a standalone repro attached.
cards.fix: server#7132 (draft): the flow route passes on whatever ffmpeg has encoded (read-any) when ICY is off, instead of waiting for a full second of encoded audio (~197 KB for FLAC). ICY framing unchanged. This restores the behaviour from before 4108ef5292 (Feb 2025, 'use static chunksize'); the single-item route already reads this way.
cards.checked: Opus subagent on origin/dev 03ee9a6872 (stable the same). The flow route reads ffmpeg output with chunk_size = icy_meta_interval if ICY else calculate_content_length(output_format) (controller.py:1546), via iter_chunked -> readexactly (helpers/ffmpeg.py:512/565, process.py:255-279), so for FLAC nothing is written until ~197 KB of encoded audio builds up. NEAR_REALTIME pacing only bursts 3 s ahead (streams/constants.py:100), so a quiet tail starves the player. Hermetic pytest repro: exact chunk size gives the first byte after 17.3 s on 20 s of silence, read-any under 3 s. ICY is off by default, so HEOS takes this path. Chunk size dates from 4bd03c2483 (Apr 2026). No fix PR. 10-22 21:06 UTC amodig on 2.11.0b6 (verified it contains #7132's chunk_size line): HEOS Denon Home 200, Tidal FLAC, no_content_length profile, balanced buffer, configured 2-speaker group with only one speaker online. Start at 410 s plays but queue progress jumps backwards and doesn't reach the next item within 85 s; start at 434 s: player/group start timeouts after ~5/10 s, group dissolved after 15 s; 'Unsupported format' errors only after his cleanup stop. Offers to dig in with GPT Astra over the weekend, asks what to test next. 10-24 amodig on b6 with both Denon Home 200s grouped: FLAC control pass, WAV Düsternis from 434 s pass, WAV full Düsternis pass, FLAC from 434 s fail (timeout, group dissolves). Matches your HEOS-buffering-on-compressed-silence read. 10-25 janoj: 'njól' (The Northerner Diaries, Tidal 91139997; Jellyfin MP3 320 too) still has ~2 short pauses in the first 10 s on b7, less than before b6.
cards.plan: Fix not confirmed. Possibly a second cause: seek start near the end of a track (434 of 466 s) + group start timeout. Second HEOS report in #6835 points at an old queue-cleanup task overlapping a new play request.

cards.checked: Opus subagent, 2.10.5 = origin/dev on this path. All library queries share one aiosqlite connection with locking_mode=exclusive (music/database.py:187, helpers/database.py:246), so one long query blocks every count and library_items call. Synthetic benchmark with the real dev schema and 64k albums: normal titles 0.03-0.18 s, 2000x "Greatest Hits" 1.1 s, 6000x 8.9 s. On HAOS with a 1.3 GB cache DB, minutes are plausible. cards.title: Sonos volume still delayed and stepped when bridged via AirPlay into a group with a Sendspin player (2.10.5, follow-up to #6110)
cards.area: server / providers/sonos + airplay (Sendspin to AirPlay bridge)
cards.summary: 2.10.5 HA add-on. A Sonos Move 2 (native SONOS preferred, AirPlay second) grouped with a Sendspin player (Echo Show 5, TECHO5 firmware) plays over the Sendspin to AirPlay bridge. Volume changes for it land 20-65 s late, one partial step per cycle, and keep stepping through old slider values after the user stopped. cards.checked: Code read on origin/dev 61842140c and 2.10.5 (identical on this path), plus cliairplay v0.5.5 and aiosonos 0.1.13. With the Sonos rendering over AirPlay, volume_control still resolves to NATIVE, so MA sends the user's volume through aiosonos setVolume and never through AirPlay. No MA-side queue fits a ~65 s cadence: the per-player VOLUME lock gives up after 30 s, the AirPlay VOLUME pipe write is non-blocking, cliairplay runs each VOLUME as one SET_PARAMETER with a 2 s budget, and nothing in airplay/sonos/sendspin/players has a 60-70 s timer. The diagnostics show the bridge restarting often, DACP server running, and one 5 s SET_PARAMETER timeout at 13:42, but no volume lines (not debug). Likely (about 35%) the Sonos itself serializes native volume while it's in an AirPlay 2 session with DACP, the same device behaviour as #6110. The timing-mode effect fits a device-side cause better than an MA one. Staying on AirPlay after the Sendspin player leaves is by design on 2.10.5. server#6675 (in 2.11.0b4) moves the group back to native sync on the next start. Not reproducible here: Sonos is off-limits at night and the cadence needs real hardware. 10-14: Opus subagent on mawi13's 10-13 test (2.10.6, Move 2 on 27.1). MA never sent a volume to Küche: every cmd_volume_set is for Echo Show 5 (its own Sendspin role, controller.py:4199-4208), Küche (AirPlay) group_volume lines are just the max-of-members display (player.py:1604-1629), and every Küche volume_level change starts as a device report (mirror triplets 19:00:40-19:07:47). mawi13's own native 25 % test via HA was held until the AirPlay session ended, so the 65 s grid is the Sonos holding native-API volume during AirPlay. MA's part: __control_for_output returns NATIVE whenever the parent supports VOLUME_SET (player.py:2468), and the AirPlay output doesn't own volume for a Sonos-linked output (airplay/player.py:935-948), so MA's own changes take the held native path too. No 60/65 s timer in MA. Nothing on dev. Their log excerpt was filtered (no DACP lines). 10-21 investigation session (your approval to post): HA's Sonos integration isn't the cause of the delay; the speaker held both MA's aiosonos change and the HA SoCo 25 % set. The 10-07 diagnostics show hass player_controls 0, so no HA entity was a volume control. The sender of Küche's 10-13 steps is unknown: an HA dashboard/automation on the HA Sonos entity, or the Sendspin bridge role path (airplay/sendspin_bridge.py _on_volume_change > AirPlayPlayer.volume_set sends VOLUME= without an owns_volume check). A solo AirPlay test removes the bridge. 10-26 11:46 UTC josiasmontag, second setup (2.10.8 Docker, Sonos Arc Ultra via MA's AirPlay player in a sync group, no Sendspin): a single volume change applies within 0.5 s; three changes 0.4 s apart do nothing for 45 s, then the Sonos reports all three via DACP within 30 ms and MA echoes each back over AirPlay. Nothing from the SONOS provider in between at Verbose. Reads as the Sonos queuing native volume changes during an AirPlay session and applying them on a fixed ~45 s tick (HA recorder shows the same 45.05 s grid). Suggests Verbose logging of outbound Sonos volume calls.

cards.title: HEOS Integration plays announcements N times
cards.area: server / heos (player provider) + streams announcement URL
cards.summary: Repeated announcements on a HEOS speaker (Denon Home 150) play 1x, 2x, 3x. HEOS `browse/play_stream` appends to the device queue and starts playback at qid 1, MA's queue cleanup always keeps the "current" entry (so one stale MA entry survives every session) and the queue-connection `get_queue` is answered ~20s late, so cleanup never catches up. Every stale entry points at the same per-player `/announcement/{player_id}.mp3` URL, which serves the new announcement, so the device plays it once per queue entry; virtual repro goes red with `[1, 2, 3]`.
cards.fix: None. The fix means bringing back HEOS queue clearing (reworked before in #3932) and depends on real-device timing, or a controller-wide announcement URL change. This needs a decision with Tommatheussen. The plan is above.
cards.checked: A/B: A=n/a B=n/a A2=n/a
cards.plan:
Checked on origin/dev 3e1d945d0. `play_media` only calls `play_url` (`browse/play_stream`, which appends). `_cleanup_heos_queue` keeps `now_playing.queue_id` and runs only while `PLAYING`. The announcement URL is stable per player (`/announcement/{player_id}.{fmt}`). So the cause holds.

Why this isn't implemented unattended:
- Option 1 (keep the max qid and `player_play_queue` to it) does not fix the captured timeline on its own. `get_queue` on the queue connection answered after ~20s, which is after the next announcement's `play_stream`, so the "newest" qid is already stale when cleanup runs. A jump mid-announcement could also cut or restart the clip. Whether that is audible can only be checked on a real HEOS device.
- Option 2 (non-blocking `player_clear_queue` on the queue connection once MA playback reaches STOP) is the likely core fix. But it brings back queue clearing, which Tommatheussen reworked several times (ghost items, then #3932 because it blocked volume commands). Whether a clear on the secondary connection is fast enough, and doesn't race the next `play_stream`, is device behaviour we can't check here.
- Option 3 (a nonce per announcement in the URL, 404 on mismatch) is a controller change that affects every player provider. A maintainer should decide that.

Proposed direction, to agree with Tommatheussen:
1. HEOS: on transition to STOP/idle while `_ma_controls_playback`, schedule `player_clear_queue` on `_heos_queue` (fire-and-forget, logged on HeosError). Cancel it if a new `play_media` starts first.
2. HEOS: in `play_media`, if a clear is still in flight, await it (with a short timeout) before `play_url`, so the new stream lands on an empty queue at qid 1.
3. Keep `_cleanup_heos_queue` for multi-item flow sessions. Optionally switch it to keep the max qid.

cards.title: DLNA: LUMIN-based renderers (TEAC NR-7CD) stay silent because MA ignores Range
cards.summary: A TEAC NR-7CD with a LUMIN network module accepts MA's DLNA stream and reports PLAYING but stays silent. The renderer reads with Range requests (bytes=0-, 12-, 16384-, ...). MA answers each one with 200 OK from byte 0 and 'Accept-Ranges: none', so the decoder gets data at the wrong offset. The reporter showed that the same bytes play fine from a server that supports Range, and has a working proxy workaround. Version 2.10.6, HA add-on.
cards.checked: DEFAULT_STREAM_HEADERS sets 'Accept-Ranges: none' (constants.py:905-913). It is used by every stream endpoint in controllers/streams/controller.py (182, 861, 1018, 1477, 1661-1685), and there is no Range handling anywhere in the streams controller. Each GET on /single/ starts a fresh pipeline from 0. Ignoring Range and sending 200 is valid HTTP, so the renderer is out of spec, but the behaviour is as described. cards.summary: 2.10.8 Docker, AudioCast AMP (generic LinkPlay) via DLNA in flow mode: after pause/resume the queue elapsed_time lags 4-6 s; the amp's HTTP curpos is right and audio doesn't rewind.

So the DLNA player's elapsed stays 0.0 with elapsed_time_last_updated reset at every resume, and the flow queue restarts from 0 on each resume (queue 12.7 -> 0.8, 16.3 -> 0.9) while the amp's HTTP curpos keeps the real flow position (9.2 s, 25.5 s, 41.8 s). Options: (a) DLNA player keeps counting from the paused elapsed when the device never reports a RelTime (no-position devices), (b) LinkPlayPlayer takes the position from the LinkPlay HTTP API (getPlayerStatus curpos) instead of DLNA. > This comment was written by Claude on Marvin's behalf

Thanks for the measurements. The code matches your reading: since 2.10.7 the shared PTP grandmaster runs on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` (airplay-cli #92), so receivers that slave to it follow the host crystal rate. > [!NOTE]
> This comment was written by Claude on Marvin's behalf

Thanks for the detailed report. The error is a bug in the Bluesound provider: when the NAD doesn't answer Music Assistant's first status request during startup, setup crashes and the player never gets added. That code didn't change between 2.10.8 and 2.10.9, so the trigger is most likely the NAD not responding in time on those two 2.10.9 starts. cards.title: Next track cut after ~30 s when the previous track is over ~7 min: inactivity monitor clears the preloaded buffer while the renderer still holds the connection
cards.summary: emilbarzin, 2.10.9 HA add-on, Denon Home 400 via HEOS with DLNA output, flow mode off: the track after one longer than ~410 s is cut at 27-31 s. Packet capture: speaker preloads the next /single/ URL (3.06 MB), stops reading ~7 min, then MA ends the response at 6.24 MB. Own code analysis + capture; offered verbose logs.
cards.checked: audio_buffer._monitor_inactivity clears a buffer once _last_access_time is >300 s old (checked every 30 s); _last_access_time only refreshes per chunk pull or is_valid(), so a reader stalled on HTTP backpressure never refreshes it. After clear(), _get raises AudioBufferEOF and get_raw_stream breaks, so the speaker gets a short valid track, logged only at VERBOSE. ~410 s threshold: prepare_next_audio_buffer at duration-60 calls is_valid() once, resetting the timer. Scratch repro (stalled reader, timeout 0.3 s) ends at 5/100 chunks; trial fix (count active readers, skip the clear while any are attached) passes it + 149 audio_buffer tests. Since #3507 (Mar 2026), not a regression; not DLNA-specific. #7306-#7308 unrelated (forced_content_length only). Side, unverified: Tidal /tidal-dash/ route lives 300 s + track, cached StreamDetails 600 s, may explain the reporter's 404 after a re-buffer. A unit test (stalled reader past the timeout still gets the whole track) would have caught it.
cards.plan: PR: count readers in get_raw_stream (try/finally), skip the inactivity clear while any are attached + regression test. Core streams buffer lifetime, so check with Marcel (#3507/#4294 author). Tidal DASH route lifetime as a separate follow-up.
cards.action: Note: the bug is core (audio_buffer inactivity clear), not DLNA-specific, so it hits any non-flow player that preloads and stalls; OzGav labelled it low-priority DLNA. Reporter also lists HEOS flow-mode problems (bit-perfect breaks, 3 s lead stutter) as separate issues. Go on the reader-count fix (`fix 6979`) or ask Marcel? Reply drafted.
cards.reply:
> [!NOTE]
> This comment was written by Claude on Marvin's behalf

Thanks, great analysis, and it matches the code. The prepared buffer for the next track is released after 300 s without reads, even while the speaker still has the connection open. The speaker then gets the end of the stream after the ~30 s already in the pipe. The ~410 s threshold comes from the next-track prepare check 60 s before the end of the current track, which resets that timer. No need for verbose logs. Until this is fixed, turning "Enable queue flow mode" back on for this player should avoid it, because the queue is then sent as one stream with no separate preload. The Tidal 404 looks like a separate issue, and we'll look at it apart from this one.

#6620 (closed, volume normalization strings) fixed by OzGav's server#6685, no backport label. It cherry-picks cleanly onto stable, so it could ride 2.10.6 if you add backport-to-stable. FtbC set 09:40.

AirPlay 2 native (#6508): a HomePod whose audio path wedges keeps answering keepalives for ~18 min before the /feedback read times out, so MA shows playing that long. Worth a watchdog on RTP/retransmit feedback once a log covers a drift onset.

appvars: the monthly Apple Music token rotation workflow failed on 09-01 and 10-01 because its validation treats HTTP 429 as a rejected token. The current token is valid until 2027-01-30, but rotation has stopped (found during #6645).
ffmpeg HTTP input has no -rw_timeout, so a blackholed CDN connection shows up as a silent 30 s "0s buffered" instead of a clear network error (found during #6642).
hass_players: ESPHome media players don't report media_position, so MA extrapolates wall-clock time and the progress/track change run ahead after a device stall (found during #6643).
#6425 leftovers after server#6609: pause briefly shows the previous pause position, and the read-back skips the artwork crossfade.

#6642 fastseek (server#6727) only covers mp3. A long TOC-less file in another container over HTTP could still stall on a deep resume. Worth a check with audiobookshelf/podcast sources once #6727 lands.

libraop _raopcl_terminate_rtp (raop_client.c:736-741) pthread_joins RTP threads that never started on every failed RAOP connect (offline speaker); ASan aborts. airplay-cli#81 skips its new make test under SANITIZE until that's fixed upstream (philippe44/libraop).

Metadata update_metadata (controllers/metadata/controller.py:304-310): handle_refresh(force_refresh) closes before the provider lookups, so a forced "Update metadata" still serves cached fanart.tv/TheAudioDB answers, empty ones included (#6659).
FFmpeg 9 verifies TLS on HLS segment requests too and -tls_verify on the input doesn't reach them, so self-signed https HLS radio still fails (#6663 notes).
AirPlay: the Sendspin bridge's RAOP-compatible connect sends MFi auth-setup and a Roku (AirTunes/377.40.00) answers RTSP 403, so bridge starts to it fail (support#6672 diagnostics).
roku_media_assistant/provider.py:83 unload iterates a dict that changes size (RuntimeError in support#6672 diagnostics).

#6679: cmd_volume_set queues every concurrent volume step behind the per-player VOLUME lock. Latest-wins coalescing (skip a call when a newer target was recorded while waiting) would help sliders and parallel automations. Not the cause of #6679.

#6627 (closed): magdalar reports on 2.10.6 that pausing an Audiobookshelf book on Sonos still jumps MA's progress back to the session start, though resume mostly continues at the right spot. Worth a new issue or a reopen.
server-worktrees/triage-6676 (fix/cue-mapping-loss, uncommitted) can go: OzGav closed #6676 as by design.
ytmusic: warn when the username field is set but isn't a 21-digit Brand Account id, it's ignored silently today (#6706).
Plex Connect: plexapi PlayQueue.create IndexError when the selected offset is outside the returned window (queue_sync.py:384, #6688 diagnostics).

Server venv in ~/git/music-assistant/server is skewed (models < 1.1.221, old aiosendspin), so the pre-commit mypy hook fails on unrelated providers. A synced venv (uv sync --extra test + requirements_all, used via UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT) passes. Refresh the main one.

#6722 gPodder Nextcloud setup: when the user entered https and Nextcloud returns an http:// poll endpoint, show a translated error pointing at overwriteprotocol instead of an unhandled ClientConnectorError (setup_flow.py _nc_start/_nc_poll).
Stream server: the 'disconnected prematurely' warning (streams/controller.py ~L1017) is meant to skip radio, yet it fired for a RadioBrowser stream in #6720. Check the duration guard.
#6725: after server#6810, check non-flow mode, where a repeat-one preload may still reset seek_position (playback_tracker.py:142).

#6739: AlbumDetails, PlaylistDetails, TrackDetails and PodcastEpisodeDetails reset to the top on history back the same way as ArtistDetails. Apply useHistoryScrollRestore to them once the #6739 PR lands.

AirPlay buffer_depth is silently ignored for RAOP (only passed for AirPlay 2 in providers/airplay/stream.py). Either hide the setting for RAOP players or document it; #6738's reporter wasted a test on it.
server#6810 (#6725 seekbar with repeat, merged 10-14 without a backport label) cherry-picks clean onto stable. Reporter confirmed and closed #6725. Add backport-to-stable if you want it in 2.10.7.

Playback tracker keeps max() of positions for the same item, so any single spurious PLAYING position from another provider sticks for the rest of the item (seen via #6749 on WiiM). Consider whether the tracker should drop one-frame jumps.
~/.musicassistant has no Tidal provider, although the triage spec says YT Music, Apple Music, Spotify and Tidal are configured there (found 10-16 via #6759). Add a Tidal account or fix the spec.
Local files logs 'Error processing <file> - ' with an empty message when the exception has no text (AssertionError in #6815). Logging the exception type would make these diagnosable at INFO level.

server#6706 (Cast artwork in a Universal Group, draft) lost its issue: #6102 was auto-closed. voc0der replied after the close (10-20 09:55 UTC) that they won't test without a docker image. Keep it as a standalone fix or close it.
#6668 (closed by you 10-20 as a tagging issue): the get_album_dir exact-tier bug for self-titled album folders still has a clean unit repro and no fix. Worth a small PR if you want it.
HA core music_assistant handle_player_config_updated defaults a missing expose_player_to_ha to True (#6822). Small HA core PR: fall back to the client player's expose_to_ha.

Squeezelite: setting the provider log level to Verbose at runtime never reaches the aioslimproto logger (set only in handle_async_init, log-level changes skip the reload). Override update_config to re-apply the level. Found on #6800, same on stable.

AirPlay: _adopt_device_volume (airplay/player.py:828-839, 1031-1044) and the Sendspin bridge volume path send VOLUME= without an owns_volume check; a candidate MA-side cause for Sonos volume snapping back during AirPlay (#6838, #6664).

aioslimproto: disconnect() returns early after _socket_reader sets _connected False (client.py:652/658 in 3.2.3, :665/671 in 3.3.0), so the old socket is never closed and sits in CLOSE-WAIT (#6800). One-line fix in aioslimproto; reproducible with plain squeezelite (kill the client, `ss -tan state close-wait '( sport = :3483 )'`).
issue-triage release_table: for an unreleased patch milestone (2.10.8) check the backport branch (backport/2.10.8), not origin/stable; 'on stable' reads as 0 until the release.

Frontend: the shuffle-off icon (two straight arrows, ShuffleBtn.vue IconArrowsRight) doesn't read as shuffle; #6757's reporter toggled Repeat thinking it was Shuffle. Small UX chip: use a crossed-arrows icon in both states, colour for on.

server: _player_options (helpers/config_entries.py:119-128) offers live private web players in plugin connected-players pickers. Agreed fix from the #6773 discussion: skip players that are both private and hide_in_ui, mirroring the frontend's groupMemberPickerVisible. Independent of #6773's answer.

Core: queue play actions hold the player's playback lock through play_index's skip loop (15 s BUFFER_READY_TIMEOUT per unplayable item), so a cmd_stop waits up to 30 s (#6840). Consider letting a stop/handoff preempt the skip loop.
